regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: This is androgen deprivation therapy (ADT): it lowers testosterone to help control prostate cancer. With radiotherapy, the aim may be cure; in advanced disease, it is part of ongoing cancer control.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Adults with advanced hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, following specialist assessment.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Relugolix blocks gonadotrophin-releasing hormone (GnRH) receptors in the pituitary gland. This lowers the signal to the testes and reduces testosterone without the initial surge seen with GnRH agonist injections. It does not normally need an anti-androgen solely to prevent a starting flare.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Relugolix 360 mg on the first day, then 120 mg once daily without planned breaks. Your specialist sets the duration and any prescribed changes.
key_points: Relugolix 360 mg on the first day, then 120 mg once daily without planned breaks. Your specialist sets the duration and any prescribed changes.

If treatment is interrupted for more than 7 days, contact the team before restarting: a new loading dose is normally needed. Some interacting medicines require a different dose or separation by at least 6 hours. Do not change the dose yourself; ask pharmacy to check every new medicine.

Additional cancer tablets, chemotherapy or radiotherapy are separate decisions based on your cancer and overall health. regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: This is androgen deprivation therapy (ADT): it lowers testosterone to help control prostate cancer. With radiotherapy, the aim may be cure; in advanced disease, it is part of ongoing cancer control.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Locally advanced or metastatic hormone-dependent prostate cancer under NCCP 00480.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Triptorelin is a GnRH agonist. It briefly raises pituitary hormone signals, then sustained exposure reduces them and testosterone falls. Unlike a receptor antagonist, it can cause an initial flare, so early symptoms and the protection plan need attention.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Triptorelin 11.25 mg is given every 12 weeks (84 days). The usual NCCP route is into a muscle; the source also permits injection under the skin for this formulation.

treatment_rationale.summary: Androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) lowers testosterone, a hormone that can drive prostate cancer. This medicine is your ADT. Keep treatment going until your team changes the plan; do not stop because prostate-specific antigen (PSA) has fallen.
